summary: Alfred Edward Housman worked in linguistics. He studied at Bromsgrove School, King Edward's School, Birmingham, and St John's College, Oxford (~1877–1881), and later held a post at University College London (~1892–1911).
Linguist Alfred Ernout held posts at the University of Lille (1913–1924), École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1924–1949), University of Paris (~1927–1949), and Collège de France (1941–1951).
Alfred Espinas worked in philosophy. He studied at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and École Normale Supérieure (~1864–1867), and held a post at the University of Paris (~1894–1912).

Alfred Forke worked in sinology and philosophy. He studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1886–1889) and the University of Geneva (~1888–1889), later holding posts at Berlin and Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen (1903–1923), and the University of Hamburg (~1923–1935).

Working in history, archaeology, Indology, and Buddhist studies, Alfred Foucher studied at École Normale Supérieure and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Sylvain Lévi. He held posts at EFEO, EPHE, and the University of Paris (1907; 1929–1936).

Alfred Gell studied at the University of Cambridge (~1965–1967) under Edmund Ronald Leach and earned his Ph.D. at LSE (~1968–1972). He taught at the University of Sussex (~1971–1974), Australian National University (1974–1979), and LSE (from 1979).

Indologist and linguist Alfred Hillebrandt earned his doctorate at the University of Breslau (~1872–1875) under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and studied at the University of Munich (~1874–1875) under Martin Haug. He held professorships at Breslau starting in 1883.

Alfred Körte worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. After studying at the University of Bonn (~1886–1890), he held posts at Greifswald, Bonn, Basel, Giessen, Freiburg, and the University of Leipzig (~1917–1934).

Indologist and linguist Alfred Ludwig studied at the University of Vienna and Humboldt University of Berlin under Albrecht Weber and others. He held a post at Vienna (1858) before serving as professor at Charles University from 1860.
Alfred Métraux studied at École des chartes, INALCO, and École Pratique des Hautes Études under Marcel Mauss (~1925–1928). He later held a post at the École Pratique des Hautes Études (~1953–1963).

Alfred Radcliffe-Brown studied at King Edward's School, Birmingham, and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1902–1909). He held posts at the University of Sydney (~1926–1931), University of Chicago (~1931–1937), University of Oxford (~1937–1946), and FESPSP (~1942–1944).

Specializing in religious studies and Indology, Ali S. Asani studied at Harvard College (~1973–1977) and Harvard University (~1977–1984). He has served as a professor at Harvard University since ~1983.
Alice Y. Tseng specializes in Japanology and history/archaeology. She was a graduate student of Eugene Y. Wang (attested 2005) and served as a professor at Boston University (attested 2013).

Alicia Turner works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2009), where her doctoral supervisors were Bruce Lincoln and Steven Collins.

Alison Denton Jones works in sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. Her teachers included Allan H. Barr, Mingfei Gao, and Margaret Dornish, and her doctoral supervisor was Martin King Whyte.

Alka Patel, a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology, earned a bachelor's at Mount Holyoke College (~1985–1989) and a PhD at Harvard University (~1993–2000). She became associate professor at the University of California, Irvine (~2007).

Allan G. Grapard specialized in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He earned a Ph.D. at INALCO (~1971–1978) and held professorships at the University of California, Santa Barbara (1985) and the University of California (~1986–2009).

Philosopher Allan Gibbard studied at Swarthmore College (~1959–1963) and Harvard University (~1965–1971). He held posts at the University of Chicago (1969–1974), University of Pittsburgh (1974–1977), and University of Michigan (1977–2016).
Sinologist Allan H. Barr earned a doctorate at the University of Oxford (until 1983). He has served as a professor of Asian Languages and Literatures at Pomona College (attested 2001).

Indologist Allen Wright Thrasher completed doctoral studies under Daniel H. H. Ingalls (~1968–1972) and studied under several traditional teachers. He held a post at the Library of Congress (~1987–2012).
